facts.raw_span: A woman in her 60s with a history of hypertension
sudden-onset chest pain
no history of any acute febrile illness
no family history of sudden cardiac death
tachycardic with a pulse of 120 beats/min
blood pressure was normal
White blood cell count: 14,300/µL
Serum calcium: within normal limits
High-sensitivity troponin I: 1.15 ng/mL
Brain-type natriuretic peptide: 1060.30 pg/mL
Initial ECG showed sinus tachycardia, PR-segment elevation in lead aVR, PR-segment depression in leads I, II, III, aVF, and V4 to V6
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT: revealed an enhanced left-adrenal heterogeneous mass measuring 4.1 × 3.4 cm

Brain-type natriuretic peptide: 1060.30 pg/mL
Initial ECG showed sinus tachycardia, PR-segment elevation in lead aVR, PR-segment depression in leads I, II, III, aVF, and V4 to V6
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT: revealed an enhanced left-adrenal heterogeneous mass measuring 4.1 × 3.4 cm

concepts.why: The patient presented with sudden-onset chest pain, tachycardia, and elevated troponin and brain-type natriuretic peptide levels, which are consistent with Takotsubo cardiomyopathy.
The contrast-enhanced abdominal CT revealed an enhanced left-adrenal heterogeneous mass, which is consistent with an adrenal adenoma.
The patient has a history of hypertension, which increases the risk of developing hypertensive heart disease.
The patient presented with chest pain, elevated troponin levels, and ECG changes, which are consistent with acute coronary syndrome.
The adrenal mass found on CT scan could be a pheochromocytoma, which is a type of adrenal gland tumor.
The patient has an elevated white blood cell count and troponin levels, which could indicate myocarditis.
The patient has an elevated brain-type natriuretic peptide level and ECG changes, which could indicate cardiac tamponade.
The adrenal mass found on CT scan could be causing adrenal insufficiency.

rationales.F01: Hypertension is a risk factor for various cardiac conditions.
rationales.F02: Sudden-onset chest pain is a common symptom of acute coronary syndrome and other cardiac conditions.
rationales.F05: Tachycardia can be a sign of various conditions, including cardiac and adrenal disorders.
rationales.F09: Elevated troponin levels indicate cardiac damage, which is consistent with several cardiac conditions.
rationales.F10: Elevated brain-type natriuretic peptide levels indicate cardiac strain, which is consistent with several cardiac conditions.
rationales.F11: The described ECG findings are consistent with several cardiac conditions, including acute coronary syndrome and Takotsubo cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F12: The presence of an adrenal mass is highly suggestive of adrenal adenoma or pheochromocytoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy is supported by sudden-onset chest pain, elevated troponin, and systolic apical ballooning on left ventriculography, with no strong contradictions.
